data.title: Cheniere Energy Shares Drop 2.8% Over 5 Days Following Suspected LNG Tanker Cyberattack
data.description:
Cheniere Energy (LNG) stock dropped 2.8% over the past five days to $270.97 as news emerged that a tanker bringing U.S. oil (CM:CL) and gas to Europe suffered a suspected cyberattack. The Vivit Africa LNG vessel picked up its gas cargo from Louisiana's Cameron LNG terminal and sailed across the Atlantic toward Italy. However, the crew lost access to internal monitoring systems while traveling through the Mediterranean Sea.

The crew reported the incident to the Korean Register, which serves as safety adviser to the South Korean-owned vessel. Trading firm Vitol Group holds the ship under a long-term lease but declined to share further details. Following the system failure, the ship idled off the Italian coast before turning away from its destination port in Rovigo to head toward Algeciras, Spain.

Maritime Authorities Are Monitoring Security Risks

The Italian Coast Guard stepped in to help after the captain reported a breakdown in cargo tracking screens. Local officials warned nearby ships to keep their distance so everyone stayed safe on the water. The ship uses control gear from Kongsberg Maritime, but company reps said it is still too early to tell what caused the system failure.

This issue follows similar security scares from late August, when U.S. officers boarded two tankers off the American coast over cyber concerns. Federal teams are now watching nearly 20 ships around the world for similar threats. Neither ship owner H-Line Shipping nor the Korean Register answered calls for comment as teams look into the event.

LNG Stock Drops on the News

Traders pushed Cheniere Energy shares down 2.8% over five days as fears grew about cyber risks across global shipping routes. While a single ship delay rarely hurts a huge gas producer, events like this point to bigger industry headaches. When hackers mess with ship systems, insurance costs rise and deliveries get delayed. Oil and gas prices also experience volatility on public markets.

If LNG's shipping lines have to spend more money fixing tech issues and checking vessels, profits take a direct hit. On top of that, choppy oil and gas prices, as well as political tensions in Europe & the Middle east, make investors nervous about owning energy stocks right now. Until safety teams clear up what happened to the Vivit Africa LNG, traders are choosing to play it safe and pull money out of the stock.

data.title: JPMorgan Chase (JPM) Abandons Oil Price Forecast as 'Redlines Crossed'
data.description:
JPMorgan Chase (JPM) has given up on its crude oil price forecast as the Iran war drags on into its seventh month. In a note to clients, Natasha Kaneva, head of global commodities strategy at JPMorgan, wrote: "For the first time since the start of the Iran conflict, we don't have a baseline view… We simply don't know how to model the endgame."

JPMorgan assumed at the start of the war that several "economic redlines" would force U.S. President Donald Trump into an agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz waterway, where 20% of the world's oil is typically transported. Those redlines that JPMorgan had forecast included crude oil prices above $100, retail gas prices near $5 a gallon, and the 10-year Treasury yield above 5%.

"Six months later, many of those lines have been crossed, yet the exit strategy is less clear, not more," said JPMorgan's Kaneva.

The U.S. and Iran had reached an interim deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in June, but that agreement quickly collapsed and fighting has resumed.

Crude oil prices are now above $100 U.S., gas prices are above $5 U.S. a gallon in many U.S. cities, and the 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5% earlier this week.

At the same time, the price of diesel fuel is above $6 U.S. per gallon, a record high.

JPMorgan notes that there are no signs from the U.S. or Iran that they're ready to de-escalate the fighting and get the Strait of Hormuz reopened,

Exacerbating the situation, Ukraine continues to strike Russian oil refineries, driving global energy prices higher.

JPMorgan estimates that the fair price for Brent crude oil, the international standard, is about $90 U.S. per barrel. But it is currently trading near $105 U.S. a barrel.

But where prices go from here, and how the Iran war ends, is anyone's guess, according to the bank.

JPM stock has gained 12% over the last year to trade at $349.31 U.S. per share.

data.title: Tobacco Giant Phillip Morris (PM) Raises Dividend 9% as It Ramps Up Shareholder Rewards
data.description:
Phillip Morris (PM) has raised its quarterly dividend by 9% as it continues to focus on shareholder rewards. Going forward, the tobacco giant will pay a quarterly distribution to stockholders of $1.60 per share, up 8.8% from the previous dividend of $1.47. The new payout gives PM stock a forward yield 3.36% based on the current share price.

Phillip Morris' next dividend is payable on Oct. 26 to shareholders of record as of Oct. 2. The latest hike continues the company's streak of increasing its dividend every year since becoming a public company in 2008. Over the past 18 years, Phillip Morris has raised its dividend a total of 248%, or by a compound annual growth rate of 7.2%.

Rewarding PM Stockholders

Phillip Morris continues to prioritize shareholder rewards. Over the last decade, Philip Morris has returned $75 billion back to its shareholders through dividends and also stock buybacks. The company has spent nearly $1 billion ($984 million) on share repurchases, in addition to ratcheting up its dividend payouts.

data.title: Microsoft vs. Alphabet: One AI Stock Gets an Upgrade, but the Sidelines Call for the Other, Says Top Investor
data.description:
Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) and Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) are reaching an interesting point in their AI spending race. Both companies are committing enormous sums to data centers and computing infrastructure, but investors are getting a different mix of businesses for roughly the same valuation. Microsoft has Azure and its enterprise software ecosystem, while Alphabet still has the huge cash-generating businesses of Search and YouTube supporting its AI push.

The valuation gap between the two has also largely disappeared. Microsoft's forward P/E is at about 23.3 times expected 2027 earnings, compared with roughly 22.9 times for Alphabet. With only a small difference between the multiples, the comparison becomes much more about the earnings each company can produce over the next few years.

That is the focus of the analysis from an investor using the pseudonym The Alpha Analyst (AA). AA previously had a stronger preference for Microsoft, but argues that Alphabet's improving growth and profitability have changed the relative setup.

That's not to say Microsoft no longer has a compelling AI opportunity. Azure is benefiting from demand for AI computing, while Microsoft can also monetize AI through products such as Microsoft 365 Copilot. Its broad enterprise customer base gives the company an established distribution channel for new AI services.

But the company is also spending heavily to build the infrastructure needed to support that demand. AA points to the scale of the company's capital investment and the pressure this can place on cloud margins. Azure can continue producing strong growth, but AA argues that Microsoft's cloud gross margins have remained relatively stagnant, making it harder for further revenue growth to translate into the kind of margin expansion investors might expect from such a large AI investment.

Alphabet presents a different combination of growth drivers. Google Cloud is expanding while its operating margins are improving, giving the business scope to contribute both additional revenue and greater profitability. AA expects Alphabet's revenue growth to exceed Microsoft's through 2027, which becomes particularly relevant when the two companies are trading at almost the same earnings multiple.

AA also highlights Alphabet's TPUs (Tensor Processing Units) as a potentially important part of the AI story. The custom chips are designed for AI workloads and can be supplied through Google's cloud infrastructure. AA believes contracted TPU system sales could provide an additional source of revenue that is not fully reflected in current expectations.

There's also Alphabet's advertising business to consider. Search and YouTube continue to generate substantial cash, giving Alphabet the financial capacity to fund its AI investments while those newer businesses develop. The company therefore does not need every part of its AI strategy to deliver immediate returns for the overall business to keep growing.

For AA, the comparison now comes down to the forward earnings setup rather than a simple valuation argument. At roughly 23.3 times expected 2027 earnings for Microsoft and 22.9 times for Alphabet, the two stocks are being priced similarly. The question is how effectively Microsoft can turn its AI infrastructure spending into profitable growth, compared with Alphabet's combination of advertising, Cloud margin expansion, revenue growth and potential TPU sales.

Bottom line, Alpha Analyst now has a clear preference. "Alphabet is upgraded to Buy as its topline growth, cloud margin trajectory, and underappreciated TPU revenue offer superior forward risk-reward versus Microsoft's," the 5-star investor said. "Microsoft is downgraded to Hold; valuation edge has closed, and capex drag plus stagnant cloud gross margins limit near-term upside despite strong monetization trends." Wall Street, however, does not see a reason to choose between the pair, with the analyst consensus rating both stocks as Strong Buys. MSFT stock is expected to gain 15% over the next year, given the average price target lands at $571.41. GOOGL's average price target clocks in at $429.31, a figure factoring in 12-month returns of 24%. (See MSFT stock forecast or GOOGL stock forecast)

data.description:

data.title: Humanoid Brains Could Make a 'Breakthrough' By Next Summer – But Don't Ask Them for a Bottle of Beer
data.description:
Humanoid robot brains are set to take a new leap next year, according to Chinese embodied AI firm Spirit AI, just not enough yet to do your washing or to share a beer with. The company said that humanoid brains are likely to achieve a breakthrough similar to that of Open AI's GPT 3.0 model, which powered ChatGPT, as soon as the middle of 2027. But that any chance of them being deployed in peoples' homes as personal assistants is at least eight years away.

Robot Brains Remain Weak

"The brain is indeed the weakest link in the complete robotics stack," Gao Yang, co-founder and ​chief scientist of Spirit AI, told Reuters. This is despite Spirit's robots having achieved a 90% success rate for simple tasks in living room environments."The next one to two years mark the initial window for ​industrial applications. Two years from now, we'll see robots deployed in commercial service settings doing simpler tasks. Entering homes is far harder than both," said Gao, who is also an assistant professor of robotics at Tsinghua University.

At present Spirit AI's Moz1 wheeled humanoid robots are deployed on production lines at Chinese battery maker CATL as well as retailer, and  investor in the startup, JD.com (JD).

When Spirit AI was founded, a robot could perform only one isolated task well, like pouring water or folding a piece of clothing," said Gao. "Today, robots operate across large spatial areas and execute continuous complex workflows."

However, robots are still finding it difficult to perfect other actions like unscrewing a bottle cap.

China Out on Top

Chinese firms dominate the humanoid robotics sector with other firms such as Unitree and Agibot, showing off the ability of their models at dancing and sporting events like the recent World Humanoid Games. RBC Capital Markets forecasts a global total addressable market for humanoids of $9 trillion by 2050, with China accounting for more than 60%. That means robots being used in the home, at work, healthcare and in defense.

However, Unitree's recent valuation slump post-IPO has raised some uncertainty over the pace and profitability of the humanoid rollout. Fears over the growth of AI and potential danger to mankind may also hold back humanoid development and increase the prospect of tighter regulations.
